pull.title: rpc: flag invalid taproot leaf control blocks in decodepsbt
pull.body:
`decodepsbt` shows each `PSBT_IN_TAP_LEAF_SCRIPT` record as-is, with no
indication of whether its control block could actually be a genuine
leaf of the input's taproot tree. `InferTaprootTree()` already checks
this, but silently skips whatever fails — correctly, since one bad
candidate among several script paths isn't an error. So a PSBT with an
unusable leaf (wrong leaf version, malformed control block, wrong
Merkle root) shows no sign of it.

This adds a diagnostic only, no signing behavior change: an optional
`control_block_warnings` array next to `control_blocks`, naming why a
control block fails. The Merkle-root check needs
`PSBT_IN_TAP_MERKLE_ROOT` (optional per BIP371); when absent, only the
other three checks run, and the help text says so.

Similar in spirit to #25513, which added the same kind of check for
`PSBT_OUT_TAP_TREE`.

## Commits

1. Unit test for `InferTaprootTree()`'s four checks (none existed).
2. Extract the checks into `CheckTapLeafCandidate()`, shared by
   `InferTaprootTree()` and `decodepsbt`.
3. `decodepsbt`'s new `control_block_warnings` field, with its
   functional test.

Written with the help of Claude Code, reviewed by the author, who is
accountable for its content.

test: cover InferTaprootTree's leaf checks

InferTaprootTree() rejects a candidate leaf that fails any of four
structural checks (leaf version, control block size, leaf-version
byte, Merkle root), but none of them had a test.

Add a two-leaf taproot tree fixture and, for each check, corrupt
exactly what it looks at and assert the whole input is rejected.

Added before the next commit's refactor, so that one needs no test
changes.

committer Ferdinando Ametrano <ferdinando@ametrano.net> 1790699879 +0200

refactor: extract CheckTapLeafCandidate

InferTaprootTree()'s four inline "Skip script records that ..."
checks have no way to report which one a candidate failed, which the
next commit needs for decodepsbt's diagnostic.

Extract them into CheckTapLeafCandidate(), returning a
TapLeafCandidateError enum (or NONE). InferTaprootTree() now calls it
and continues on anything but NONE; its behavior is unchanged.

Declared in script/interpreter.h/.cpp, next to the Taproot constants
and hash helpers it's built from -- rpc/rawtransaction.cpp already
includes that header, so decodepsbt needs no new dependency.

merkle_root is std::optional<uint256>, not a plain uint256: decodepsbt
can lack PSBT_IN_TAP_MERKLE_ROOT and still run the other three checks.
InferTaprootTree() always has one, so this is not a behavior change
for it.

rpc: flag invalid taproot leaf control blocks

decodepsbt echoes each PSBT_IN_TAP_LEAF_SCRIPT record as-is.
InferTaprootTree() already checks whether a control block could be a
genuine leaf, but silently skips whatever fails -- correctly, since
one bad candidate among several script paths isn't an error. So a
PSBT with an unusable leaf gives no visible sign of it.

Add an optional "control_block_warnings" array next to
"control_blocks", naming why a control block fails
CheckTapLeafCandidate(). A passing control block gets no entry, and
the array is omitted entirely when every one passes; "control_blocks"
itself is untouched.

The Merkle-root check needs PSBT_IN_TAP_MERKLE_ROOT (optional per
BIP371); when absent, only the other three checks run, and the help
text says so, so an unflagged block is never overstated as verified.

No change to signing: this is decodepsbt-only.

Includes a functional test exercising control_block_warnings end to
end, on a genuine two-leaf taproot tree (needed for a real Merkle
branch to corrupt): all four checks, one passing control block, and
PSBT_IN_TAP_MERKLE_ROOT omitted from the input. The size check uses an
oversized control block, not an undersized one, since PSBT
deserialization already rejects an undersized or misaligned control
block before decodepsbt runs -- the undersized case is covered
directly at the InferTaprootTree() level instead.
